title: Life Strategies — Satisficing
metadata_mapping: Canonical frontmatter uses the existing entity schema. Richer recommendation metadata remains in this sidecar; the current search index does not automatically ingest these queries.

patterns.title: Satisficing
patterns.short_description: Define what an acceptable option must provide, then stop searching when one meets that standard.
use_when: A useful acceptance standard can be stated and verified.
An adequate option is available but further possibilities keep extending the search.
Comparing more alternatives consumes attention or delays the benefit of choosing.
A bounded task needs an explicit completion threshold.
goals: Choose an option that serves the actual purpose
Give search a usable stopping rule
Preserve important requirements while releasing optional comparisons
mechanisms: Specify an aspiration level as checkable acceptance conditions
Search sequentially and stop when an option meets the standard
Review thresholds when evidence changes or the search yields no acceptable option
not_ideal_when: The acceptance standard omits something important or cannot yet be verified.
A small, known set of options can be compared reliably at little additional cost.
Exhaustion or an attractive candidate is being used to excuse an unmet requirement.
The person needs to clarify the purpose before setting a threshold.
example_user_queries: I found something suitable but I keep looking for a better option.
How do I know when I have done enough research to choose?
Every time I compare options I add another thing I want.
I spend more time picking tools than using them.
We keep debating places to meet and never arrange the meeting.
What would count as good enough for this particular decision?
I want a stopping rule without abandoning my real requirements.
How do I separate what I need from nice extras?
I keep polishing a small task long after it serves its purpose.
What should I do if nothing meets the standard I set?
I worry that an unseen option will always be better.
When is more comparison actually worth the time?

practice.format: Optional individual reflection using the existing Pattern Language renderer
practice.boundary: Records requirements, evidence, and a user-selected next move. It does not verify facts, recommend a candidate automatically, or perform a transaction.

visual.reason: Concrete sequential-search examples explain the stopping rule without suggesting measured option scores or a guaranteed optimum.
visual.concept_graphic: A sequence of inspected candidates ends at the first accented candidate that reaches an ink acceptance boundary; two gray candidates remain beyond the search endpoint.

sources.title: Herbert A. Simon, A Behavioral Model of Rational Choice (1955)
sources.supports: Satisfactory alternatives, limited information and evaluation, and changing aspiration levels during search.

sources.title: Artinger, Gigerenzer, and Jacobs, Satisficing: Integrating Two Traditions (2022)
sources.supports: Definition and decision-environment-dependent effectiveness; reviewed the publisher abstract, not the full article.

patterns.evidence_boundary: A practical adaptation of a decision framework. The desk, venue, and notice examples are original scenarios. No guarantee of happiness, absence of regret, or universally superior choice is claimed.
